BiblicalUsage: This Aramaic ten is the ten of Daniel's visions and of the return from exile. The fourth beast has ten horns, and the ten horns are ten kings that shall arise, and at the dedication of the house of God the returned exiles offer twelve he goats for the twelve tribes of Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ten horns on a beast is a picture of power divided and crowned, ten kings who will rise and fall in their season. And the twelve he goats at the dedication say the other side of it: God's people are counted whole, tribe by tribe, and I hold that His counting outlasts every horn.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
